purpose: Triage 85 differing URLs as distinct from 85 proven citation faults; preserve provenance and avoid source substitutions that change the claim scope.
methodology: Provisional desk classification against exact-revision paragraph ledger and its research notes, without independently reopening all URLs. Classification may be revised after source-level comparison and EN/FR claim certification. Seven high-priority target URLs and accessible original pages then received direct source-scope spot-checks. These spot-checks confirmed five citation-scope defects; they do not certify the full EN/FR prose. Five citation-scope defects have been repaired using custodian or bishops' heritage pages; 85 original discrepancies remain documented, 80 still differ in current draft. BeWeB pages were indexed but direct fetches returned 403 to inspection client; this limitation is recorded. Two additional previously unresolved high-priority claim-source citations repaired: Lisieux Carmelite archival transfer, and Betania 1991 episcopal clarification. Twelve host/path/language pairs were independently checked as equivalent source pages, not errors, and kept in historical provenance. Thirteen section-specific source-quality improvements were made across five guides (Heiloo, Cornillon, Święta Lipka, Brezje, Orvieto), without assuming that every general/custodian homepage was demonstrably false. Twelve additional source pairs were adjudicated after directly reviewing the exact draft sentences and their original institutional links. In each, the originally cited source was the better match; alternative research URLs remain supplementary and no visitor citation was changed. All 85 original source URL differences now have a documented research disposition: seven earlier and four newly repaired citation-scope defects, 23 source-quality upgrades, 12 URL equivalences, 33 retained paragraph-appropriate citations and five explicit inaccessible-source holds. This is not independent EN/FR sentence-level approval. Earlier seven-defect counters updated to twelve repaired citation-scope defects, preserving the difference between a broken/mis-scoped citation and an untrue historical sentence. Some source judgments rely on custodian-indexed evidence and are not complete independent direct-URL reinspection. Follow-up on 12 November: the Frielingsdorf 2026 expired detailed parish article has been replaced by the parish's accessible dated index; the Rome Diocese's 19 October notice supersedes April Santa Croce closure language. Remaining five access-held paragraphs are not certified. On 12 November, five previously inaccessible citations were replaced at research stage with directly inspected, distinct institutional sources (Vatican Jubilee Santa Croce booklet for 2, Braga municipal Sameiro for 1, UNESCO Holy Sepulchre physical sites for 1, Greek Orthodox Patriarchate Status Quo for 1). Original inaccessible URLs and old triage comparisons remain provenance. All five remain without independent English/French, second-editor or owner approval. On 12 November, two draft guides (Toulouse Jacobins and Heraklion Saint Titus) received institutional-source-grounded narrative rewrites in EN/FR, leaving the original citation classifications, evidence holds and approvals unchanged; exact guide fingerprints and ledger were refreshed. Visitor-copy cleanup on 2026-11-12 modified 11 guide paragraphs (map/database jargon and stable-vs-changing practical access language), synchronizing their exact guide revisions in the 672-row evidence register; citation case dispositions and human release authority remain unchanged. Eight institutional source pages were directly inspected for paragraph-specific dated claims (guide orders 57, 60, 63, 66, 72, 74, 201 and 204). Eight YEAR_NOT_EXPLICIT_IN_SOURCE_SUMMARY prompts were cleared at research level, leaving 38; this is NOT paragraph or EN/FR editor certification and does not authorize publication. A 2004 Ghana News Agency announcement corroborates Kumasi basilica status while the Holy See decree remains uninspected; the repetitive Vilnius 201 wording was simplified. Final consolidated date-evidence research pass on 12 November directly compared 25 additional dated claims to named site, pilgrimage-organiser, diocesan and Holy See records, bringing direct date checks to 33 of 46 previously under-specified source-summary rows; 13 remain held at claim-level research priority. Verifying a single date never certifies the full sentence, French translation, supernatural authenticity, relic identification, current access, or publication approval.
publication_policy: No automatic guide citation rewrites, publication, PR merge, or fabricated approvals. All 224 drafts remain held until independent claim/EN/FR approval, mobile-image QA, and one exact-revision owner authorization.
